headline: The German robot maker Agile Robots is training its machines by filming workers perform tasks, to make up for a shortage of training data.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct; a Bloomberg report on a training method, resting on the CEO's own statements.
importance_line: Factory workers' own movements are becoming training material for the robots that may share their jobs; the company's figures are its own and the article does not show results from robots trained this way.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as carried by The Star, that Agile Robots' "Robot Academy" has workers film themselves so the footage captures how their hands and fingers move, then combines it with other data so robots can practise in simulation, chief executive Zhaopeng Chen said on 8 Oct 2026 at an event in Turin. The company says it has deployed more than 20,000 systems and raised $1.5 billion, and the report says a lack of training data is holding back robots in factories.
notes: Original Bloomberg link kept as url; text read on The Star's copy, which credits Bloomberg.
